en: fry the rice before adding liquid

does: Fries raw, well-drained long-grain rice in hot fat until the grains turn opaque and then pale gold, before any liquid goes in.
how: Rinse the rice and drain it well, shaking off as much water as you can, so that it fries instead of steaming.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a wide pan over medium heat and add the rice.
Stir often, scraping the bottom, as the grains turn chalky white and then pale gold.
Add the sauce or liquid as soon as the rice smells toasty, before it browns further.

cues.text: The grains turn opaque, then the colour of pale straw, and slide freely in the pan.
A dry, sandy rustle as you stir.

mistakes.mistake: Frying wet rice, which clumps and steams.
mistakes.fix: Drain it well, and let it sit in the sieve a while before frying.

mistakes.mistake: Taking the rice dark brown, which makes it bitter and hard.
mistakes.fix: Stop at pale gold and add the liquid at once.

variant_of.differs: The rice is taken further, to pale gold, in more fat, and a blended tomato sauce follows instead of wine and stock.
